title: Whole Turkey (frozen)

drivers.name: Price increase (6.1%)
drivers.evidence: Easter week 2026 (price $29.20) sold 5 units (vs baseline 5.7); no lift seen in prior high-price weeks. Noise-adjusted promotion lift is x1.0.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median of 5.7 is unchanged by events or promotions this week. The price is elevated by 6.1% (to $29.20), which historically has suppressed demand: past high-price weeks (Easter 2026, 2025) saw only 5–6 units vs baseline 5.7, with no uplift. The noise-adjusted effect of promotions is x1.0, indicating no reliable lift. The classical model’s x1.0 is correct—no drivers justify a move. The price increase is a demand deterrent, but evidence is weak and inconsistent. The baseline already reflects seasonal decline (trend -78.8% over 13 weeks), so no upward adjustment. Final multiplier shrinks toward 1.0 due to thin evidence.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-100% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
